title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own mathematics. It is page 23 of a typed Bourbaki draft (rédaction n° 380), filed in the cote among unrelated sheets. The neighbouring pages are Grothendieck's handwritten notes on Hodge and de Rham comparison and on Barsotti isogeny. The page opens '§ 2. Calcul fonctionnel holomorphe', subsection 1, 'Homomorphisme O(Sp(x)) → A': the Riesz–Dunford holomorphic functional calculus in a Banach algebra A. It corresponds to Bourbaki, Théories spectrales, Ch. I, §4 (published 1967). Following Bourbaki's style, Cauchy contour integrals are replaced by integrals against compactly supported complex measures.

Lemma 1. Let K ⊂ ℂ be compact and V an open neighbourhood of K. There is a compactly supported measure ρ on V \ K and an open neighbourhood W ⊂ V of K such that, for every holomorphic f: V → E (E a Banach space) and every z ∈ W, f(z) = ∫ f(t)/(z−t) dρ(t). Concretely, dρ = −(1/2πi) dt along a cycle in V \ K winding once around each point of K. This is the vector-valued Cauchy formula.

Lemma 2 (dual version at infinity). Let L be compact and U an open neighbourhood of L. There is a compactly supported ρ on U \ L and an open neighbourhood W of ℂ \ U such that every holomorphic F on ℂ \ L vanishing at ∞ satisfies F(z) = ∫ F(t)/(z−t) dρ(t) for z ∈ W. This is Cauchy's formula on the exterior domain; the contour at infinity contributes nothing because F(∞) = 0.

Lemma 3 (uniqueness). Let 𝔇 be a compactly supported measure on Ω = ℂ \ K whose Cauchy transform ∫ d𝔇(t)/(z−t) vanishes for z near K. Then ∫ F d𝔇 = 0 for every holomorphic F on Ω vanishing at ∞.

Proof (begun on this page). Choose a relatively compact open U ⊃ K that misses supp 𝔇 and on which the Cauchy transform vanishes. Apply Lemma 2 with L = K to get ρ supported in U ∩ Ω, so that F(z) = ∫ F(t)/(z−t) dρ(t) for z ∉ U, in particular on supp 𝔇. Then Fubini gives ∫ F d𝔇 = ∫ F(t) [∫ d𝔇(z)/(z−t)] dρ(t). The inner integral is minus the Cauchy transform of 𝔇 at t ∈ U, hence zero.

Role of the lemmas: Lemma 3 shows the functional calculus f ↦ ∫ f(t)(x − t)^{-1} dρ(t) does not depend on the representing measure. Taking F(t) = (x − t)^{-1}, which is holomorphic off Sp(x) and vanishes at ∞, this yields a well-defined homomorphism O(Sp(x)) → A.
errors: Lemma 2 as typed says 'fonction holomorphe F sur ℂ − K'. It should read ℂ − L; this is a slip in the original typescript.

Implicit requirement in Lemma 2: W must be disjoint from supp ρ (fine, since W can be taken inside ℂ \ (L ∪ supp ρ)). Also, the formula should hold for z in the unbounded components, which is guaranteed by the choice of cycle.

Lemma 3 proof: the exterior point z ranges over supp 𝔇 ⊂ ℂ \ U. One needs supp 𝔇 contained in the region where Lemma 2's formula holds (a neighbourhood of ℂ \ U), which the construction provides. The swap of integrals is legitimate since 1/(z−t) is bounded on supp 𝔇 × supp ρ, and the sign convention (z−t versus t−z) is harmless because the inner integral vanishes.

ideas.what: Cauchy integral formula expressed via a compactly supported measure, for Banach-valued holomorphic functions near a compact set
ideas.modern_name: Vector-valued Cauchy integral formula / Runge-type representation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cauchy; Banach-valued version: Dunford, Taylor (1940s–50s); measure formulation Bourbaki

ideas.what: Uniqueness lemma: a measure with vanishing Cauchy transform near K annihilates holomorphic functions on the complement vanishing at infinity
ideas.modern_name: Well-definedness of the Riesz–Dunford functional calculus

deep.surprise_reason: This is a page of a Bourbaki draft (rédaction n° 380) on the standard holomorphic functional calculus, essentially as published in Théories spectrales. It contains no Grothendieck-specific or novel content. It sits in the cote only as scrap paper: the archive page number 56 is written on it, and the neighbouring pages are unrelated notes on crystals and Hodge theory.
transcription_corrections: Bottom-left handwritten '56' (archive numbering) is omitted from the transcription.
The image indeed reads 'F sur ℂ −K' in Lemma 2; this is a typo in the original for ℂ − L, not a transcription error.
In Lemma 3, '𝔇' renders a script/stylised D in the typescript; the exact glyph is uncertain but it is a measure.
